subject: DPA follow-up: Clarifying breach-notify window, subprocessor notifications, and retention exceptions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lawson <anna.lawson@clarifyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:15:00 -0400
Subject: DPA follow-up: Clarifying breach-notify window, subprocessor notifications, and retention exceptions

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups we promised to confirm: 

- Breach notification window: You asked whether Redwood will commit to a 48-hour initial notification to Clarify Health for confirmed data breaches involving customer data. Our standard language is 72 hours for confirmed incidents, but we can evaluate a 48-hour SLA for customers with contracted SLAs and an associated security review.

- Subprocessor notification: You also asked whether we notify customers before onboarding new subprocessors that might access customer data. We publish an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and notify customers of changes; we do not currently provide a prior approval flow for every onboarding event unless the customer has a contractual requirement.

- Retention exceptions for scoped PII: For the scoped analytics logs you described (hashed device IDs + metadata), we typically have a 90-day retention by default but can configure longer retention with contract language and controls for deletion on export.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll attach a one-page DPA summary and our current subprocessor inventory for your legal/security review.
2) Ben (security) and Marissa (contracts) will follow up with proposed contract language for breach notification and a short checklist for subprocessor notification options.
3) If it helps, we can route a redline of the DPA via DocuSign for tracked approvals.

Any corrections to the summary above? If not, would your security and legal folks prefer we loop them in now or after we send the summary attachments?

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

From: Anna Lawson <anna.lawson@clarifyhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: Clarifying breach-notify window, subprocessor notifications, and retention exceptions

Thanks, Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 48-hour notify: Clarify Health requires an internal 48-hour notification SLA to begin our triage and regulator reporting activities. If Redwood can commit contractually to a 48-hour "initial notification" (status + scope + remediation plan) and then follow-up as incidents evolve, that would meet our requirement.

- Subprocessors: For any subprocessors that will have access to cleartext PHI or linkable identifiers, we need prior written notice and a 14-calendar-day review period. For lower-risk subprocessors (e.g., telemetry collectors that only receive aggregated telemetry), an after-the-fact notification is fine.

- Retention: We need the ability to extend the analytics retention window to 18 months for a scoped dataset tied to a pilot program; please advise what the operational impact/cost delta would be.

Looping in our security and legal teams on this thread — Anna (me), please see security@ and legal@ on cc. Happy to set a short call if that helps.

Best,
Anna

--
Anna Lawson
Director, Product Privacy & Compliance | Clarify Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Anna Lawson <anna.lawson@clarifyhealth.com>, security@clarifyhealth.com, legal@clarifyhealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: Clarifying breach-notify window, subprocessor notifications, and retention exceptions

Thanks Anna — appreciate the specificity. Internal notes for our recommended approach: 

- 48-hour initial notice: Security is comfortable committing to a contractual 48-hour "initial notification" that contains scope, affected datasets, and mitigation steps, provided Clarify accepts a 30-day root-cause report window and limits on preliminary forensic detail to avoid jeopardizing investigations. We will propose language to that effect.

- Subprocessor prior notice: We do not currently offer prior approval for every subprocessor, but we can commit to: (a) prior notice + 14-calendar-day review for subprocessors that will access linkable identifiers or cleartext customer data, and (b) after-the-fact notification for low-risk processors. We'll capture classification criteria in the DPA addendum.

- Retention/18-month: Ops estimates approx +18% cost for keeping the scoped analytics dataset at 18 months vs 90 days given current storage and indexed query patterns. We can provide more granular cost per GB and options (tiered retention, compressed cold storage).

Marissa, can you draft the proposed contract snippets for the three bullets (notify SLA, subprocessor prior notice clause, retention amendment) and attach the current subprocessor inventory? I'll also prepare a short security note describing what we can and can't share during early investigations.

Ben

--

Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: Clarifying breach-notify window, subprocessor notifications, and retention exceptions

Hi all — attaching a short DPA summary and our current subprocessor inventory for review (files attached). Below are proposed redline snippets you can consider including in an addendum: 

1) Initial Notification SLA: "Redwood will provide initial written notification to Customer within 48 hours of confirming an incident involving Customer Data. Initial notification will include a summary of scope, affected data categories, and interim remediation actions. A substantive root-cause report will follow within 30 days."

2) Subprocessor Prior Notice: "For any subprocessor reasonably expected to access cleartext Customer Data or linkable identifiers, Redwood will provide prior written notice and a 14-calendar-day review period. For lower-risk subprocessors, Redwood will provide notice within 10 business days after onboarding."

3) Retention Amendment: "Customer may request an alternate retention schedule for scoped datasets. Redwood will provide a written cost estimate and operational impacts within 5 business days of request. Agreed retention will be reflected in an annex to the DPA."

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v2.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.xlsx

If these look good, Soojin — please confirm whether Clarify wants the redline DPA sent via DocuSign once Anna's legal team confirms, or whether you'd prefer an editable track-changes doc first.

Marissa
